tips.title: The pronoun matches the subject
tips.body: *Je **me** lève, tu **te** lèves, il **se** lève, nous **nous** levons, vous **vous** levez, ils **se** lèvent.* The reflexive pronoun always matches the person doing it. *Je se lève* is the error, and it is common — say the pair *je me, tu te, il se* until it is automatic.

tips.title: Me, te, se elide before a vowel
tips.body: *Je m'habille, tu t'amuses, elle s'appelle.* Before a vowel or silent *h*, *me / te / se* lose their *e* and take an apostrophe. *Nous* and *vous* never change.

tips.title: The negative goes round pronoun and verb together
tips.body: *Je **ne** me lève **pas** tôt.* *Ne* comes before the reflexive pronoun, *pas* after the verb. The pronoun stays glued to its verb.

tips.title: En semaine versus le week-end
tips.body: *En semaine, je me lève à sept heures, mais le week-end je me lève à dix heures et demie.* One contrast, two times, and the whole routine topic in a single sentence. *En semaine* is *on weekdays*.

tips.title: Se lever has an accent in most forms
tips.body: *Je me **lève**, tu te **lèves**, il se **lève**, ils se **lèvent*** — but *nous nous **levons**, vous vous **levez***. The *è* appears wherever the ending is silent. *Se promener* does the same: *je me promène, nous nous promenons*.

why.matters: Getting up, washing, getting dressed, going to bed: the verbs of a daily routine are the ones French does to itself, with an extra pronoun in front of the verb that matches the subject. The topic exists because that pronoun is the first piece of French word order that English has no equivalent for, and because daily routine comes up in picture-task conversations and in listening and reading texts. Learn the pronoun here and it comes back in the perfect tense, in the infinitive after *je vais*, and in the feelings topic next year.

examples.title: The morning in six verbs
examples.body: Waking, getting up, showering, dressing, breakfast: four of those five are reflexive in French, and the odd one out, *prendre le petit-déjeuner*, is the one English speakers get right by accident. Said in order with the clock, *je me réveille à sept heures, je me lève, je me douche, je m'habille*, it is a paragraph any picture of a bedroom can prompt, and the weekend version adds the phrase every French teenager knows, *faire la grasse matinée*, to have a lie-in.

visual.alt: A table of six morning actions in order with their French verbs, four of them reflexive and two not, ending with the weekend lie-in

examples.title: The pronoun that matches the subject
examples.body: *Se lever* changes twice as you go down the table: the pronoun follows the subject, *je me, tu te, il se, nous nous, vous vous, ils se*, and the accent on the stem appears everywhere except *nous* and *vous*. One mismatched pronoun makes the sentence wrong however good the rest is, and the elided forms before a vowel or silent *h*, *je m'habille*, are the same rule wearing an apostrophe. The picture of stem and endings makes both patterns visible at once.

visual.alt: A conjugation table of se lever in the present with the reflexive pronoun before each form and the accented stem lèv everywhere except nous and vous

examples.title: En semaine, le week-end
examples.body: The same verbs told twice make a contrast worth marks: *en semaine je me lève à sept heures, mais le week-end je me lève vers dix heures*. The contrast is the structure the writing task rewards, and the negative shows control, with *ne* before the pronoun and *pas* after the verb: *je ne me couche pas tôt*. Add the sequencers and a time, and a weekday and a weekend fill the word count on their own.

steps.title: Les verbes réfléchis
steps.body:
A **reflexive verb** is one you do to yourself — wash yourself, get yourself up. French marks it with an extra pronoun in front of the verb.

*Se lever* (to get up): *je **me** lève, tu **te** lèves, il / elle / on **se** lève, nous **nous** levons, vous **vous** levez, ils / elles **se** lèvent*.

The pronoun **matches the subject**: *je → me, tu → te, il / elle / on → se, nous → nous, vous → vous, ils / elles → se*.

Before a vowel or silent *h*, *me / te / se* become **m' / t' / s'**: *je m'habille* (I get dressed), *tu t'amuses*, *elle s'appelle*.

**Daily-routine verbs**: *se réveiller* (to wake up), *se lever*, *se laver, se doucher* (to shower), *se brosser les dents, s'habiller, se coucher* (to go to bed), *se reposer* (to rest), *se détendre* (to relax), *s'amuser* (to have fun), *se promener* (to go for a walk), *se coiffer, se maquiller*.

The verb itself conjugates as normal — most are regular *-er* verbs. *Se lever* and *se promener* add an accent (*lève, promène*) except in *nous* and *vous*.

steps.title: Ma routine du week-end
steps.body:
The weekend routine contrasts with the weekday one, and the contrast is the point.

**En semaine** (on weekdays): *je me réveille à six heures et demie, je me lève à sept heures, je me douche, je m'habille vite et je prends le bus.*

**Le week-end**: *je fais la grasse matinée* (I have a lie-in), *je me lève vers dix heures et demie* — 3.5 hours later — *je me détends, je me promène avec mon chien, je me couche tard*.

**Times**: *à sept heures, à sept heures et quart, et demie, moins le quart; vers* (around); *tôt* (early), *tard* (late).

**Sequencing**: *d'abord, ensuite, puis, après, enfin*. *D'abord je me lève, puis je me douche, ensuite je prends mon petit-déjeuner.*

**Non-reflexive parts of the routine**: *je prends mon petit-déjeuner* (have breakfast), *je quitte la maison* (leave the house), *je rentre à la maison* (come home), *je fais mes devoirs, je regarde la télé*.

**Questions**: *Tu te lèves à quelle heure ? À quelle heure est-ce que tu te couches ?* The pronoun stays in front of the verb in a question too.

steps.title: Les autres personnes, et le passé
steps.body:
**Other people's routines** use the same verbs with the matching pronoun.

*Mon frère **se** lève à midi le dimanche. Mes parents **se** couchent tôt. Nous **nous** promenons ensemble. Vous **vous** levez à quelle heure ?*

**Talking about the family together**: *on se lève, on se détend, on s'amuse* — *on* is the everyday *we*, and it takes *se*.

**Reflexives in the perfect tense** take **être**, and the participle agrees: *je **me suis** levé(e), elle **s'est** couchée, ils **se sont** amusés*. *Samedi dernier, je me suis levé à onze heures et je me suis bien amusé.* One exception: when a body part follows the verb, the participle does not agree — *elle s'est brossé les dents*.

**Reflexives with an infinitive** keep the pronoun with the infinitive, and it still matches the subject: *je vais **me** coucher tôt, je dois **me** lever à six heures, j'aime **me** détendre*. Not *je vais se coucher*.

**Opinions about routine**: *je déteste me lever tôt*, *j'adore faire la grasse matinée*, *c'est fatigant, c'est relaxant, c'est ennuyeux*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write the six forms of *se lever*.
2. Translate: *I wake up at half past six.*
3. Write *I get dressed* and *she is called* with the elided pronoun.

**Part B.**

4. Write your weekday getting-up time and your weekend one, contrasted with *mais*.
5. Write *I do not go to bed early* with the negative in the right place.
6. Describe a family member's routine with *il / elle se …*

**Part C.**

7. Write what you are going to do this weekend with *je vais me …*
8. Write what you did last Saturday morning with *je me suis …*
9. Write six sentences: a weekday routine with two times, the weekend contrast, a negative, a reflexive with an infinitive, and an opinion.

For question 9, check every pronoun against its subject.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Match the pronoun to the subject, always.** *Je me, tu te, il se, nous nous, vous vous, ils se.* One mismatch and the sentence is wrong even if everything else is right.

**Elide before a vowel or silent h.** *Je m'habille, elle s'amuse, tu t'appelles.* Writing *je me habille* is a visible slip.

**Put the negative round the pair.** *Je ne me couche pas tôt.* *Ne* before the pronoun, never between the pronoun and the verb.

**Keep the accent on lève.** *Je me lève, ils se lèvent* — but *nous nous levons*. The pattern is the same as *acheter → j'achète* and *se promener → je me promène*.

**Contrast weekday and weekend.** *En semaine … mais le week-end …* is the content of this topic; a routine with no contrast is a list.

**Use the perfect for last weekend.** *Je me suis levé tard, on s'est bien amusés.* Reflexives take *être* and usually agree, as *je suis allé* does (not when a body part follows: *elle s'est brossé les dents*).

**Keep the pronoun with the infinitive.** *Je vais me coucher, je dois me lever, j'aime me détendre.* The pronoun still matches the subject even though the verb is an infinitive.

**Add a reason and an opinion.** *Je me couche tard le samedi parce que je sors avec mes amis, et c'est génial.*

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- Reflexive verbs carry a **pronoun matching the subject**: *me, te, se, nous, vous, se*.
- *Je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons, vous vous levez, ils se lèvent.*
- **m' / t' / s'** before a vowel or silent *h*: *je m'habille, elle s'appelle*.
- Routine verbs: *se réveiller, se lever, se doucher, s'habiller, se coucher, se reposer, se détendre, s'amuser, se promener*.
- *Faire la grasse matinée* — have a lie-in.
- **Negative**: *je **ne** me lève **pas***.
- **Times**: *à sept heures et demie, vers dix heures, tôt, tard*.
- **En semaine … mais le week-end …**
- Sequencers: *d'abord, ensuite, puis, après, enfin*.
- **Perfect** with *être* and agreement: *je me suis levé(e), on s'est amusés*.
- **Infinitive** keeps its pronoun: *je vais me coucher, je déteste me lever tôt*.
- *Se lever, se promener*: accent except in *nous / vous*.

questions.prompt: Why is it **je vais me coucher** and not *je vais se coucher*?
options: The pronoun matches the subject je, even before an infinitive
Se is only used after aller in the third person plural
Me is the infinitive form of the reflexive pronoun

questions.solution: The reflexive pronoun agrees with the **subject** of the sentence, not with the infinitive. *Je* → *me*: *je vais **me** coucher*, *tu vas **te** coucher*.

examTechnique.body:
Match the reflexive pronoun to the subject every time, elide it before a vowel or silent *h*, and wrap *ne … pas* round pronoun and verb together. Give times, sequence with *d'abord, ensuite, puis*, and contrast **en semaine** with **le week-end**.

For range, use a reflexive in the perfect (*je me suis levé(e)*) and one before an infinitive (*je vais me coucher, je déteste me lever*).
examinerErrors: Nous nous lèvons with an accent.
J'ai me levé instead of je me suis levé.
A routine with no times and no contrast.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer matches every reflexive pronoun to its subject across several persons, elides before vowels, keeps the accent pattern of *se lever* right in *nous* and *vous*, and places the negative round the pair. It contrasts weekday and weekend with times and sequencers, uses the reflexive perfect with *être* and agreement for last weekend, keeps the pronoun with an infinitive after *aller*, *devoir* or an opinion verb, and adds a reason and an opinion.
